en.title: Luca Guadagnino's 'American Psycho' Adaptation Now in Limbo
en.summary: Fans hoping to see Luca Guadagnino's take on Bret Easton Ellis's notorious novel 'American Psycho' will have to wait, as the director has cast significant doubt on the project's future. Lionsgate remains tight-lipped, but the director's recent comments suggest the film is far from a priority.
en.body:
The chilling prospect of **Luca Guadagnino** reimagining the iconic, blood-soaked world of **American Psycho** seems to be fading into uncertainty. Fans have been keenly awaiting the director's take on **Bret Easton Ellis**'s controversial novel, a project that has been in development with Lionsgate. However, recent statements from Guadagnino himself have poured cold water on immediate expectations, suggesting the film is not moving forward anytime soon.

When pressed about the status of the **American Psycho** adaptation, Guadagnino offered a non-committal response that has left the project in limbo. While Lionsgate has not officially declared the film dead, the director's words, "Maybe one day I would do it," indicate that it's no longer on his immediate radar. This comes after **Scott Z. Burns** penned a script for the new take, which was famously adapted into the 2000 film starring **Christian Bale**. Actor **Drew Starkey** had previously been rumored for the pivotal role of Patrick Bateman and confirmed he had read the script, adding to the anticipation that has now been tempered by Guadagnino's latest update.

## The Lingering Shadow of Bateman

The possibility of Guadagnino directing **American Psycho** had generated considerable excitement within film communities worldwide. Known for his evocative and sensuous filmmaking in works like *Call Me By Your Name* and *Suspiria*, his approach to the dark satire and visceral violence of Ellis's novel promised a unique and potentially groundbreaking cinematic experience. The very idea of his artistic sensibilities being applied to the meticulous, psychopathic world of Patrick Bateman sparked intense debate and speculation about casting, tone, and visual style. The current ambiguity leaves a void where eager anticipation once stood, with fans left to ponder what might have been, or if that "one day" will ever arrive.

## What's Next for Guadagnino

While the future of **American Psycho** remains uncertain, **Luca Guadagnino** is far from idle. He recently premiered his drama *Artificial*, which explores the world of AI and stars **Andrew Garfield**, at the New York Film Festival on October 5. This project, along with other potential endeavors, seems to have taken precedence over the Patrick Bateman story for the time being. Fans will be watching to see which of his announced or rumored projects will materialize next, even as the door for *American Psycho* remains ajar, albeit barely.
